text:
Carla: Quick Q — how should we prioritize smoke tests vs the full bench during model onboarding? The deep benches keep taking days and often block rollouts :thinking:
Ben: We should split lanes: fast-lane for interface/compat + small quality probes, and deep-lane scheduled async on low-pri capacity. Fast-lane gates the canary release.
Alice: +1. Fast-lane should catch compile/IO/kvcache regressions and large perf outliers. Something like: compile_ok, kvcache_pass, smoke_quality_delta < 0.08.
Dan: Also need a separate check for quantized variants. Some ops only fail under int8 paths. Fast-lane should surface op-coverage gaps.
Eva: Operationally we can do fingerprinting + replay of a 1k-sample subset on a small cluster. If that fails -> block. If it passes, push to staged canary with soft-fallback.
Carla: Example config for discussion:
```yaml
onboard_lanes:
  fast:
    timeout: 30m
    probes: 5
    metrics: [latency_p50, latency_p95, smoke_quality_delta, token_cost]
  deep:
    timeout: 12h
    benches: [full_eval, stress_throughput]
    samples: 10000
```
Ben: Add a stability_window: run the fast probes 3 times and require variance < 10%. That reduces flakiness causing false blocks.
Alice: For canary routing: if fast-lane passes, auto-enable canary tag with small traffic and a rollback policy: if quality regresses > threshold or latency spikes, auto-fallback to previous model.
Dan: Concern: tiny probes can miss corner-case latency cliffs. Mitigate with adaptive sampling: expand sample set if any metric is near threshold. Also include a tiny set of 'golden inputs' that exercise edge ops.
Carla: Good point. We should define signal tiers: blockers (compile, crash, op-mismatch), high-priority regressions (quality delta > X, p95 latency > Y), advisories (cost increase, p50 shift).
Eva: I'll sketch the follow-up RFC: fast-lane implementation, probe selection heuristics, stability_window semantics, and scheduling policy for deep benches. @Carla want me to own the draft? :thumbsup:
Carla: Please do. I'll own fast-lane infra changes (prober + admission).
infra-bot: Scheduled job 2925010400 for deep bench (low-priority queue).
Ben: One more ops detail — attach provenance (git hash, quantization profile, kernel list) to every onboarding artifact so debugging is reproducible.
Alice: Agree. Also expose the fast-lane outputs in console with per-route breakdown so product teams can inspect regressions quickly.
Dan: I'll prepare a short checklist of op-coverage tests we need for int8 paths and post it to the RFC thread.
Carla: Nice. Let's aim to land the RFC this sprint and +1 on implementation plan.
Eva: Will open the PR with config schema and a small prober change early next week.
Carla: Thanks all.
